name: Curtiss Robin
manufacturer: Curtiss Aeroplane and Motor Company / Curtiss-Wright
summary: Late-1920s high-wing cabin monoplane famous for record endurance flights; 769 were built.

wings: High-wing monoplane braced by a pair of parallel diagonal struts per side
Early models had large flat fairings over the struts
engines: Nose-mounted engine (OX-5 V-8, Challenger or Wright radial), often with cylinders exposed
fuselage: Enclosed cabin seating three, two passengers side by side behind the pilot

tellTales: High-wing monoplane braced by parallel diagonal struts
Boxy three-seat cabin with an exposed-cylinder engine
Fixed tailwheel gear on an early high-wing monoplane

confusedWith.howToTell: The Reliant has a single strut per side and a gull wing; the Robin has two parallel diagonal struts and a straight wing.
The Monocoupe is smaller with two seats and a reverse-curve rear fuselage; the Robin seats three in a longer cabin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
